entities.name: Cephisodotus the Younger
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cephisodotus the Younger (born c. 355 BCE, Athens; died c. 300 BCE), an eminent sculptor of the late Classical and early Hellenistic periods, stands as a crucial link in the artistic lineage of Athens, inheriting and evolving the stylistic innovations of his renowned father, Praxiteles. Operating primarily in Athens, a vibrant center of artistic and intellectual life, Cephisodotus contributed significantly to the sculptural landscape through his bronze and marble works, many of which adorned public spaces and religious sanctuaries. His career unfolded during a transformative era, as the political dominance of the Athenian city-state waned and the broader Hellenistic world began to emerge under the influence of Alexander the Great's successors, prompting shifts in artistic patronage and thematic focus.

Working alongside his brother, Timarchus, Cephisodotus is credited with several notable commissions, although many are known primarily through literary sources and later Roman copies. Among his most celebrated works was a portrait of the orator Demosthenes, commissioned after Demosthenes' death in 322 BCE. This bronze statue, known through multiple Roman marble copies, notably in the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, is praised for its psychological depth and realistic portrayal, marking a departure from earlier idealized forms. He also collaborated on a group depicting the Muses and a statue of the poet Menander, further illustrating his versatility and engagement with contemporary intellectual figures. His pieces often featured a delicate balance between the idealized forms of the High Classical period and the emerging naturalism and emotional complexity characteristic of the Hellenistic age.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cephisodotus the Younger played a crucial role in the transition from Classical to Hellenistic sculpture, particularly through his development of psychologically nuanced portraiture and his preservation of Athenian artistic excellence into a new era.
